summary: Both supplied occurrences are already represented. PrS 41/10 repeats the inherited road-watch construction cited prs 113/2; 29/357 is the exact existing reconnaissance passage. No new example, stem or form is necessary.

ʕal-persons at PrS 41/10 identifies companions for whom watch is kept, rather than an enemy being spied on. The joint-return agreement makes a protective reading available from context; the gloss is clarified without splitting the sense already used for this example.

The Preterit reconnaissance has an ensuing seeing/possible-ambusher clause, while Infectum prospectively undertakes watch along the road. Neither use supports a Detransitive or a distinct light-verb construction.
The etymological alternatives in the head, Arabic ǧss versus a Turoyo ǧasūs denominative, remain unresolved; these two contexts cannot decide between them.
Please reconcile inherited prs 113/2 with supplied PrS 41/10 before changing the citation.

Is ʕal in the protective watch formula regularly benefactive, or does it identify the persons kept under watch with protective purpose supplied by context? The current evidence supports the protective gloss but not a general coding rule.
